Analysis: Croatia, who have drawn their last three
matches, must win in Greece on Wednesday to keep
alive their fading hopes. Denmark should beat
Slovenia in Copenhagen, and look set to overhaul
Greece at the top of the table with home and away
matches against Bosnia in June and August.

Analysis: Scotland's victories over Estonia and
Austria a month ago put them in a commanding
position -- but they have played two matches more
than Austria or Sweden. If Scotland win in Sweden
on Wednesday, it is hard to see them losing their
lead -- especially as face Belarus (home and away)
and Latvia in their last three matches.

Analysis: Spain, Yugoslavia and Slovakia now look
to be in a three-way hunt. The Czechs, less
than a year after finishing runners-up in Euro' 96
are all but eliminated. Wednesday's match is vital
to both Yugoslavia and Spain, who look favourites
to occupy the top two positions.
